A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Driver-WM study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across appendix and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original AIDE forecasting and semantic-recognition results, architectural ablations, intervention experiments, and three-seed evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds direct-ground-truth intervention errors, oracle external-latent experiments, and a risk-ranking analysis in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The frozen Qwen3-VL interface, dual-stream transitions, gated contextual injection, ST-GCN decoder, and training objectives are retained. The oracle settings and output-derived risk scores are supplementary diagnostics; the proposed forecasting procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds the task of ranking future high-motion events using Driver-WM outputs on the existing AIDE test population. AIDE forecasting and semantic tasks, the High-Motion subset, and optional Drive&Act pretraining are retained; no new dataset or population is evaluated.

E2.justification: The existing benchmark and classification-reference comparator sets are unchanged. New Tables 11–12 introduce eval-only and train/eval teacher-forced oracle comparisons and motion-only versus semantics/uncertainty-augmented risk scores. Here, motion-only denotes a score derived from Driver-WM predictions, not an additional motion-forecasting baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate intervention errors against ground truth on HM at h=5, distinguish eval-only oracle inputs from train/eval teacher forcing, and assess risk ranking with AUROC, AUPRC, and recall at 10% FPR. Risk components use validation-set normalization. The original splits, 5→5 rollout, and benchmark training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F add focused analyses of whether interventions reduce predictive accuracy, whether external-latent drift limits forecasting, and whether semantics and uncertainty improve risk ranking. These extend the existing AIDE analysis while retaining the architectural ablations, robustness checks, and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Both versions already report means and standard deviations over seeds 42, 123, and 456. v2 adds a paired-bootstrap test for the risk-ranking AUPRC gain, reporting a 95% confidence interval of [0.013, 0.094] and p=0.0009. No increase in training-run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–9 retain their results. New Table 10 reports HM h=5 errors of 164.48 px without external context and 226.55 px with the gate disabled, versus factual 155.82 px. Table 11 adds oracle results of 157.85 and 152.19 px under distinct oracle protocols. Table 12 reports composite versus motion-only risk AUPRC of 0.1785 versus 0.1364; these are added comparisons, not improvements over v1 under an unchanged method setting.

T1.justification: The transition definitions, gating equations, physical priors, latent losses, and Gaussian/KL derivations retain their mathematical substance. Section 3.4 displays the previously stated physical-prior formula and compacts the latent-loss equations without introducing new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The three main contributions remain traffic-conditioned driver rollout, directionally gated dual-stream dynamics, and a frozen-VLM interface with unified decoding. The condensed abstract and revised conclusion preserve these claims; the new diagnostics supply supporting evidence rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes factual-rollout sensitivity from ground-truth accuracy, interprets the oracle results as suggesting an internal-dynamics/coupling bottleneck, and states image-plane calibration limits. Appendix A replaces asserted planning benefits with potential downstream uses requiring validation, while Appendix F explicitly limits its safety evidence to a risk-ranking proxy.

D1.justification: The added appendices document intervention evaluation without retraining, the oracle teacher-forcing arrangements, and risk-score ingredients, including seed variance and validation-statistic normalization. Existing feature-extraction instructions, hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and the project-page link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 41 to 66 works, with broader coverage across the introduction and related work. Additions include unified planning/generation models, CausalDrive, egocentric hand-trajectory conditioning, and further VLM adaptation, reasoning, and navigation research. This substantially expands literature coverage while retaining the driver-centric positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted revisions to the abstract, related work, loss explanations, results discussion, conclusion, and Appendix A. It inserts Appendices D–F and renumbers the former D–E as G–H. The main narrative organization and most existing technical text are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables for the new diagnostics, renumbers the notation table from 10 to 13, and reformats some loss equations. Figures 1–5 and existing table structures are retained, with limited pagination and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: Table 10 strengthens the intervention argument by adding actual ground-truth errors where v1 relied on deviations from factual predictions. The oracle and statistically assessed risk-ranking diagnostics add useful evidence, and Appendix A more accurately qualifies planning applications. The improvement remains limited: the safety result is a high-motion proxy, and Section 4.3 still incorrectly describes the 15.2-pixel factual deviation as an error increase.
